topics.topic: Meaning, Nature and Sources of Nigerian History: Oral tradition, archaeology, and written chronicles
learningObjectives: Define history as the scientific and systematic study of past human activities and societal evolution
Distinguish between primary sources (artifacts, eyewitness accounts, oral traditions) and secondary sources
Explain the importance of archaeology, radiocarbon dating, and linguistics in reconstructing pre-colonial Nigerian history

topics.topic: Centers of Ancient Civilization in Nigeria: Nok culture and terra-cotta sculptures
learningObjectives: Locate Nok culture sites in present-day Kaduna State dating from 900 BCE to 200 CE
Analyze Nok artistic techniques: stylized human heads, perforated eyes, and elaborate coiffures
Examine the antiquity of Nok iron smelting furnaces and its transformative impact on agriculture and weaponry

topics.topic: Centers of Ancient Civilization in Nigeria: Igbo-Ukwu bronze casting and burial chambers
learningObjectives: Detail the archaeological excavations by Thurstan Shaw at Igbo-Isaiah, Igbo-Richard, and Igbo-Jonah (9th century CE)
Examine the sophisticated lost-wax (cire perdue) bronze castings: roped bronze pots, altar stands, and ceremonial vessels
Analyze the socio-religious significance of the Eze Nri divine kingship institution evidenced in burial finds

topics.topic: Centers of Ancient Civilization in Nigeria: Ife and Benin bronze and terra-cotta art traditions
learningObjectives: Examine naturalistic terra-cotta and brass heads of ancient Ife and Oduduwa dynastic traditions
Trace the historical transmission of brass casting traditions from Ife to Benin through master craftsman Igueghae
Analyze royal Benin court art: commemorative Oba heads, Queen Mother Idia ivory masks, and palace brass plaques

topics.topic: Pre-Colonial State Systems: Kanem-Borno Empire (Sayfawa Dynasty and Mais)
learningObjectives: Trace the founding and 1000-year continuity of the Sayfawa dynasty in the Lake Chad basin
Analyze administrative and military reforms under Mai Dunama Dibbalemi and Mai Idris Alooma
Examine the economic foundations of Kanem-Borno: trans-Saharan trade routes, cavalry warfare, and Islamic diplomacy

topics.topic: Pre-Colonial State Systems: The Hausa States (Hausa Bakwai and Banza Bakwai)
learningObjectives: Analyze the Bayajidda legend and the historical classification into Hausa Bakwai (seven authentic states) and Banza Bakwai
Examine the political administration of Hausa kingdoms: Sarki, Galadima, Madawaki, and territorial district heads
Explore the commercial and craft supremacy of Kano (textile dyeing, leatherwork) and Katsina as learning hubs

topics.topic: Mid-Term Continuous Assessment & Museum Artifacts Interpretation Drill
learningObjectives: Assess pupil mastery of historical methodology, Nok, Igbo-Ukwu, and northern pre-colonial state systems
Analyze photographs of Nigerian archaeological artifacts under examination conditions
Remediate common student errors in distinguishing bronze from terra-cotta and lost-wax casting steps

topics.topic: Forest Kingdoms and Coastal City-States: The Old Oyo Empire (Alaafin, Oyomesi, and Ogboni)
learningObjectives: Trace the founding of Old Oyo (Oyo-Ile) by Oranmiyan and its military cavalry expansion
Analyze the sophisticated constitutional system of checks and balances between the Alaafin, Oyo Mesi (Bashorun), and Ogboni cult
Examine reasons for the collapse of Old Oyo: Afonja’s rebellion, Fulani incursions, and internal constitutional conflicts

topics.topic: Forest Kingdoms and Coastal City-States: The Benin Empire and the Eweka Dynasty
learningObjectives: Trace the transition from the Ogiso dynasty to the Eweka dynasty founded by Prince Eweka I
Analyze the warrior warrior-kings (Oba Ewuare the Great, Ozolua, and Esigie) and imperial expansion to Lagos and the coast
Examine Benin’s administrative structure: Uzama council of kingmakers, palace chiefs, and town chiefs

topics.topic: Pre-Colonial Decentralized State Systems: The Igbo, Tiv, and Ibibio societies
learningObjectives: Explain the political dynamics of decentralized ('stateless' or republican) governance in pre-colonial Nigeria
Analyze decision-making in Igbo society: village assemblies (Oha), title societies (Ozo), age grades, and council of elders
Examine the egalitarian socio-political organization of the Tiv people based on segmentary lineage systems

topics.topic: Trans-Saharan Trade: Trade routes, commodities (salt, gold, slaves), and impacts on Nigerian societies
learningObjectives: Map primary trans-Saharan caravan trade routes connecting Kano, Borno, and Ghat to North African Mediterranean ports
Examine main trade commodities exchanged: horses, salt, glassware, leather goods, kola nuts, and gold
Evaluate the profound cultural, religious, and economic impacts: introduction of Islam, Arabic literacy, and currency

topics.topic: Comprehensive Termly History Revision & Essay Construction Seminar
learningObjectives: Review cumulative themes across ancient civilizations, centralized empires, and republican societies
Practice constructing structured analytical essays conforming to WASSCE History Paper 2 standards
Refine student capability in contextualizing pre-colonial institutions within modern Nigerian national identity
Administer official SSS 1 History theory and objective examination
Grade scripts according to WAEC standardized historical analysis marking rubrics
Record and publish official continuous assessment and examination grades
